assertion_analysis.fails_if: The final current-stage marker is removed or no longer names the final stage.
The current or completed start timestamp is omitted or comes from a different tick.
The finish timestamp is absent, stale or differs from the independent fixture clock.
The heartbeat disappears or becomes unparsable; this assertion alone does not prove that heartbeat time advances.
Timing records disappear, stage keys are omitted, stage intervals are attributed incorrectly, or durations from successive ticks are accumulated instead of replaced.
The total differs from the sum of controlled work intervals or the session-free reader omits the persisted total.
The reader cannot find a valid local store or reports a completed fresh tick as non-live.
The completed tick remains marked running.
Slowest-stage selection picks any stage except the fixture interval of four seconds.
The slowest interval is omitted, uses the wrong unit or differs from the independent four-second work interval.
The completed session-free station reading cannot be loaded.
Entering a subsequent tick fails to publish the new current stage or makes the local reading unavailable.
The subsequent tick start is not updated or running age is computed incorrectly from the controlled wall clock.
Starting a subsequent tick erases or overwrites the preceding completed record; both reads are separate JSON-decoded snapshots.

assertion_independence: The durations dictionary is used by fixture work stubs to advance a fake monotonic clock and by expectations; it is never supplied as a timing record to Station. Reinstating the missing-record defect raises KeyError in all three tests. No assertion compares an output to the same timing value passed into the implementation.
